release_notes.headline_internal: Worktree timeout responses are now truthful, actionable, and bounded
highlights: Clamped callers are no longer advised to raise a timeoutMs that was just clamped away; remediation is mode-aware and never names an option the current mode ignores.

Removed the hardcoded "poisoned workflow" diagnosis and unconditional adv_doctor referral from adv_worktree_cleanup, adv_worktree_delete, and adv_worktree_detach — all three race a setTimeout sentinel with no error to classify, so the claim was always a guess.
Cleanup timeouts now report the stage in flight plus pendingDeleteCount, and distinguish an unreadable pending-delete queue from an empty one.
Added skipDiscovery for drain-only recovery of already-queued deletes, replacing manual `git worktree remove` as the recovery path. Documented in the /adv-cleanup contract.

Bounded every git subprocess on the cleanup discovery path below the 8s tool budget, closing a rq-worktreeBoundedCleanup02 conformance gap where two shared helpers ran at 30s and 10s. Non-cleanup callers keep their original defaults.
Added the missing C6 regression guard: corrupting the worktree/index.ts git default previously passed all 65 tests in the touched suites.
